decisions.choice: the LORD answers Job
decisions.reason: For the first time since the prologue God speaks, and he answers Job himself, not the friends or Elihu. Job had asked for exactly this: "Call, and I will answer, or let me speak, and you reply" (13:22; 31:35). The divine name, used in the prologue and only once in the speeches (12:9), returns here. As with the other speech introductions (3:1-2; 9:1), these words are prose and the speech that follows (38:2-40:2) is poetry.

decisions.choice: the storm: a violent windstorm
decisions.reason: The word means a storm of wind, a tempest (Psalm 107:25, 29; Jonah 1:4, 12). It is not necessarily a spinning wind, which the traditional "whirlwind" suggests. God often appears in storm and wind (Psalm 18:8-16; Ezekiel 1:4; Nahum 1:3), and Elihu has just described a storm gathering (37:1-13, 21-22). The LORD answers from the storm again at 40:6.

decisions.choice: answered (B), spoke to (R), without "and said"
decisions.reason: Hebrew introduces speech with two verbs, "answered and said". Literal keeps both; Balanced and Readable say it once, as in the other speech introductions of Job.

decisions.choice: «la tempestad»
decisions.reason: The word is a storm of wind (m2); «torbellino», familiar from older Spanish Bibles, suggests a spinning wind.

decisions.choice: « répondit et dit » (L), « répondit » (B): passé simple; « a parlé » (R): passé composé
decisions.reason: The speech introduction is narrative: French narrative uses the passé simple at Literal and Balanced and the passé composé at Readable. God's speech that follows is in the tenses of speech.

decisions.choice: « la tempête »
decisions.reason: The word means a violent windstorm, not necessarily a spinning wind (m2); « tourbillon » is the traditional French rendering and suggests a whirlwind.

decisions.choice: "dhoruba"
decisions.reason: A violent windstorm (m2); "kisulisuli" is a whirlwind, which the Hebrew does not necessarily mean.

decisions.choice: "cơn bão"
decisions.reason: The word is a windstorm (m2); "gió lốc" / "gió trốt" would say a whirlwind.

decisions.choice: "폭풍"
decisions.reason: A violent windstorm (m2); "회오리바람" says a whirlwind, and "폭풍우" adds rain the word does not name.

decisions.choice: do meio do redemoinho, the same words in 38:1 and 40:6
decisions.reason: For the whole book: one wording for the two openings of the LORD's speeches. "Redemoinho" is the Portuguese word readers know for the wind God speaks from, and it names a violent wind; m2 notes that the Hebrew word is a windstorm that need not spin, so this is marked uncertain, and "tempestade" is the alternative a reviewer may prefer.

decisions.choice: counsel: God's plan, the purpose with which he orders the world
decisions.reason: The word ('etsah) means advice, plan or purpose. Here it is the purpose with which God made and governs the world, which the rest of the speech displays (38:4-39:30); Job has called God's counsel his own (12:13). Job repeats the question in 42:3 and owns that he spoke of things too wonderful for him.

decisions.choice: this: Job
decisions.reason: Since Elihu has just finished, some have taken "this" to be him. But verse 1 says the LORD answered Job, the challenge of verse 3 is addressed to Job, and Job takes the words to himself in 42:3.

decisions.choice: darkens counsel by words without knowledge: obscures the plan by speaking ignorantly
decisions.reason: To darken is to make unclear. Job's words, spoken without knowing what God knows, have hidden God's purpose instead of showing it. The charge is ignorance, not wickedness: God does not say Job lied (compare 42:7).

decisions.choice: my plan (B), my plans (R)
decisions.reason: "Counsel" today usually means advice. Balanced and Readable say "plan" and supply "my", since the speaker is God and the plan is his (m1).

decisions.choice: God speaks to Job in 해라체 with 나 and 너, naming himself without -시-
alternatives: 하오체 (as between Job and his friends)
decisions.reason: As God's speeches elsewhere in the Old Testament, God speaks down to Job in the plain style (누구냐, 하여라). The 하오체 of Job's dialogues is kept for speakers addressing an equal; it is not used for God.

decisions.choice: gird up your loins: get ready for action or a contest
decisions.reason: People wore long robes, and before running, working or fighting they tucked the skirt into the belt (1 Kings 18:46; 2 Kings 4:29; Jeremiah 1:17). The phrase means: be ready for a hard task. God repeats it in 40:7.

decisions.choice: like a man: like a strong man, a warrior
decisions.reason: The word (gever) often means a man in his strength, a fighting man. God calls Job to stand up and face him as Job wanted (13:3, 22; 23:3-7; 31:35-37).

decisions.choice: I will ask you, and you answer me: the roles of the hearing reversed
decisions.reason: Job asked God to let him speak and to answer him (13:22). Now God takes the questioner's part, and the speech is built of questions (38:4-39:30).

decisions.choice: Get ready like a fighter
alternatives: Gird up your loins like a man
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (m1) and gives the warrior sense of the word for "man" (m2).

decisions.choice: "[jibu]"
decisions.reason: Swahili "unijulishe" needs something to make known; the bracket matches the English "[it]".

decisions.choice: God calls himself "Ta" and Job "ngươi"
decisions.reason: God addresses Job from above, as in his rebukes in Isaiah and Jeremiah; "Ta" takes the deity_pronoun span in mid-line, a line-initial "Ta" is written plainly.

decisions.choice: God speaks to Job with "tu" (38-41), with "te", "teu" and the verb in the second person singular
decisions.reason: For the whole book: God speaks to one person with "tu" (docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md; JOB_NOTE), as he does to the accuser in 1-2 and to Eliphaz in 42:7. It also sets his words apart from the friends' and Elihu's "você", so the reader hears that a different speaker has taken the stand.

ko.L: 내가 땅을 세울 때에 너는 어디 있었느냐? \q 네가 깨달음을 안다면 말하여라.

ko.R: 내가 땅을 제자리에 놓을 때 너는 어디 있었느냐? \q 네가 안다면 나에게 말해 보아라.

pt.L: Onde estavas tu quando eu fundei a terra? \q Declara, se tens entendimento.
pt.B: Onde estavas tu quando eu lancei os fundamentos da terra? \q Diz-{{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, se tens tanto entendimento.
pt.R: Onde estavas tu quando eu coloquei a terra no seu lugar? \q Explica-{{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, se entendes disso.

decisions.choice: founded the earth: the earth pictured as a building
decisions.reason: Verses 4-7 describe creation as the building of a house: foundations, measurements, a measuring line, footings and a cornerstone (Psalm 104:5; Proverbs 8:29; Isaiah 48:13). Job was not there to watch the builder.

decisions.choice: if you know understanding: if you really understand
decisions.reason: "To know understanding" means to have insight (Proverbs 4:1). The condition is ironic: the questions show that Job does not have it (compare verses 5, 18 and 21).

decisions.choice: Tell me (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "tell" without an object; English needs one, and the hearer is God.

decisions.choice: « quand j'ai fondé »
decisions.reason: God's speech uses the tenses of speech; the passé composé also keeps the line clear of the familiar Segond wording.

decisions.choice: "Onde estavas tu", with the pronoun written out after the verb
decisions.reason: Portuguese normally drops the subject pronoun, but the question puts Job in sharp contrast with God's "eu" in the same line (m1), so the pronoun is written out. Drafted from the Hebrew: Literal keeps the single verb "fundei"; Balanced spells out the builder's picture with "lancei os fundamentos".

decisions.choice: for you know: surely you know (irony)
decisions.reason: The short clause can be read as a condition ("if you know") or as an exclamation ("for you know!"). Either way it is ironic: God is asking about something only the builder could know.

decisions.choice: a line: a builder's measuring cord
decisions.reason: The word (qav) is the cord a builder stretched out to measure and to keep a wall straight (Isaiah 28:17; Zechariah 1:16). It continues the picture of the earth as a building.

decisions.choice: a measuring line (B), a builder's line ... to measure it (R)

decisions.choice: bases: the footings a building stands on
decisions.reason: The word ('eden) is used of the bases or sockets that held up the frames of the tabernacle (Exodus 26:19-25). The earth is pictured as a building whose footings are sunk into something; God asks what that something is.

decisions.choice: cornerstone: the first stone of a building
decisions.reason: The cornerstone fixed the line and level of the whole building (Isaiah 28:16; Psalm 118:22). Laying it was a moment for celebration, as when the foundation of the second temple was laid with singing and shouting (Ezra 3:10-11), which verse 7 describes.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs into verse 7
decisions.reason: The question continues: "who laid its cornerstone, when the morning stars sang together?" Literal and Balanced end the verse with a comma; Readable makes two sentences.

vi.L: khi các ngôi sao ban mai cùng nhau ca hát \q và hết thảy các con trai của Đức Chúa Trời reo hò?

vi.R: Đó là lúc các ngôi sao buổi sớm cùng hát với nhau \q và mọi đấng ở trên trời reo hò vui mừng.

ko.L: 새벽 별들이 함께 노래하고 \q 하나님의 아들들이 모두 환호하던 그때에?

ko.R: 그때 새벽 별들은 함께 노래했고 \q 하늘의 존재들은 모두 기뻐서 소리쳤다.

pt.B: enquanto as estrelas da manhã cantavam juntas \q e todos os filhos de Deus soltavam gritos de alegria?
pt.R: Isso aconteceu enquanto as estrelas da manhã cantavam juntas \q e todos os seres celestiais gritavam de alegria.

decisions.choice: the morning stars: the stars seen just before dawn, here as heavenly beings
decisions.reason: The morning stars are the bright stars still visible at dawn. Set beside the sons of God, they are pictured as living beings who praise their Maker, as the stars and the angels are called to praise him in Psalm 148:2-3.

decisions.choice: the sons of God: heavenly beings, as in 1:6
decisions.reason: The phrase means the heavenly beings who serve God; see the decision at 1:6. They were present when the earth was founded, and Job was not.

decisions.choice: shouted: a loud shout of joy and acclaim
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the shout that greets a king or celebrates a victory, and of the shout when a foundation stone is laid (Ezra 3:11; Zechariah 4:7). Creation began with a celebration.

decisions.choice: the heavenly beings (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 1:6, Readable says who they are; Literal and Balanced keep "the sons of God".

decisions.choice: It happened while (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable ends verse 6 with a question and starts a new sentence here, so it supplies "It happened" to tie the scene to the laying of the cornerstone.

decisions.choice: as estrelas da manhã; os filhos de Deus (L, B), os seres celestiais (R)
decisions.reason: "Os filhos de Deus" and Readable's "os seres celestiais" are the wording of 1:6 and 2:1, so the reader meets the same heavenly beings (m2). "Estrelas da manhã" is the plain phrase for the stars seen at dawn (m1); "da alva" is older literary Portuguese.

decisions.choice: and [who] shut in: the question "who" carries on
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "and shut in". The questions of verses 5-6 ("who ...?") carry on, so "who" is understood; the answer, as in verses 9-11, is God.

decisions.choice: the sea's birth: the sea pictured as a newborn
decisions.reason: The sea bursts out of the womb like a child at birth, and God acts as the one who clothes it and wraps it (verse 9). In the old poems the sea is a wild power, but here it is God's infant, and he sets its limits (Psalm 104:9; Proverbs 8:29; Jeremiah 5:22).

decisions.choice: [who]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies "who" in brackets to show the question continues (m1).

pt.R: Eu o vesti com nuvens \q e o enrolei em nuvens escuras, como um bebê num cobertor.

decisions.choice: swaddling band: the strips of cloth a newborn was wrapped in
decisions.reason: Newborn babies were rubbed with salt and wrapped tightly in strips of cloth (Ezekiel 16:4). God wraps the new sea in cloud and darkness as a mother or midwife wraps a baby.

decisions.choice: thick darkness: heavy, dark cloud
decisions.reason: The word ('arafel) is the dense dark cloud in which God dwells (Exodus 20:21; 1 Kings 8:12). The fog and cloud that lie on the sea are its baby clothes.

decisions.choice: like a baby in a blanket (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the swaddling band with a familiar picture and starts a new sentence.

decisions.reason: « maillot » is the old word for a newborn's swaddling bands and names the single band of the Hebrew; « langes » would be the plural cloths.

ko.R: 나는 바다에 한계를 정해 주고 \q 빗장과 문을 달아 그것을 막았다.

pt.L: e quebrei para ele o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} limite \q e pus tranca e portas,

pt.R: Eu lhe pus um limite \q e coloquei trancas e portas para segurá-lo.

decisions.choice: broke: marked out, cut out (a boundary)
decisions.reason: The verb usually means "break". With "my limit" it seems to mean that God cut out a boundary for the sea, as a coastline is broken into the land. The early Greek translation has "set", and some think of God breaking the sea's force. The sense of the whole line is clear: God set the sea a limit.

decisions.choice: my limit: the boundary God decrees
decisions.reason: The word (choq) means a decree and so a fixed limit. It is used of the sea's boundary in Proverbs 8:29 and Jeremiah 5:22, and of the laws of the heavens in verse 33.

decisions.choice: a bar and doors: the sea pictured as shut in a house
decisions.reason: City and house gates were closed with doors and barred with a beam (Deuteronomy 3:5; Nehemiah 3:3). The picture of verse 8 continues: the sea is kept behind barred doors.

decisions.choice: marked out (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense m1 takes; Literal keeps "broke" so the reader can see the unusual verb.

source.text: וָאֹמַ֗ר עַד־פֹּ֣ה תָ֭בוֹא וְלֹ֣א תֹסִ֑יף וּפֹ֥א־יָ֝שִׁ֗ית בִּגְא֥וֹן גַּלֶּֽיךָ׃

en.L: and I said, 'To here you may come, and no farther, \q and here [a limit] will be set for the pride of your waves'?
en.B: and said, 'You may come as far as this and go no further; \q here your proud waves will halt'?
en.R: I told it, 'You can come up to here, but not beyond. \q Here is where your proud waves stop.'

sw.R: Niliiambia, 'Unaweza kufika mpaka hapa, lakini si zaidi. \q Hapa ndipo mawimbi yako ya kiburi yanaposimama.'

vi.L: và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} phán: 'Đến đây ngươi được đến, và không thêm nữa, \q và tại đây [giới hạn] sẽ được đặt cho sự kiêu ngạo của các ngọn sóng ngươi'?
vi.B: và phán: 'Ngươi chỉ được đến đây, không được đi xa hơn; \q các ngọn sóng kiêu căng của ngươi phải dừng lại tại đây'?
vi.R: Ta đã bảo nó: 'Ngươi được đến chỗ này thôi, không hơn nữa. \q Sóng kiêu ngạo của ngươi phải dừng lại ở đây.'

ko.L: 내가 '여기까지는 와도 되지만 더는 안 된다. \q 여기서 네 물결의 교만에 [한계가] 정해질 것이다' 하고 말했을 때에?
ko.B: 내가 '너는 여기까지만 오고 더는 나아가지 마라. \q 네 거만한 물결은 여기서 멈추어라' 하고 말했을 때에?
ko.R: 나는 바다에게 말했다. '여기까지는 와도 된다. 그러나 더는 안 된다. \q 네 거만한 물결은 여기서 멈춘다.'

pt.L: e disse: 'Até aqui virás, e não mais adiante, \q e aqui [se porá um limite] ao orgulho das tuas ondas'?
pt.B: e disse: 'Até aqui podes vir, e não além; \q aqui as tuas ondas orgulhosas vão parar'?
pt.R: Eu lhe disse: 'Podes vir até aqui, mas não além. \q É aqui que as tuas ondas orgulhosas param.'

decisions.choice: will set: an impersonal verb, "one will set", that is, a stop will be set
alternatives: here it shall stop (a different reading of the verb)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "and here one will set in the pride of your waves", with no object. It is best read as impersonal: here a limit is fixed. Some suggest a slightly different verb, "here it will stop"; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: the pride of your waves: the sea's arrogant force
decisions.reason: The sea's rising waves are pictured as pride, a rebel lifting itself up. God rules "the raging of the sea" (Psalm 89:10) and stills it (Psalm 65:8). The sea goes no further than God allows.

decisions.choice: not add: go no further
decisions.reason: "You will not add" means you will not go on, you will not go further (compare 40:5).

decisions.choice: a limit will be set (L); will halt (B); stop (R)
decisions.reason: English needs an object or a plainer verb for the impersonal "one will set" (m1).

decisions.choice: "tu" for the sea ("virás", "as tuas ondas")
decisions.reason: God speaks to the sea as poetry speaks to things that cannot answer, with "tu" (as Job speaks to the earth in 16:18); it is the same form God uses to Job in these chapters, and "você" would sound like conversation.

source.text: הְֽ֭מִיָּמֶיךָצִוִּ֣יתָ בֹּ֑קֶר יִדַּ֖עְתָּה הַשַּׁ֣חַרמְקֹמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: From your days have you commanded morning? Have you made know the dawn its place,

en.L: In your days have you commanded the morning? \q Have you made the dawn know its place,
en.B: Have you ever in your life given orders to the morning \q or shown the dawn its place,
en.R: Have you ever once in your life told the morning to begin? \q Have you shown the dawn where to appear,

es.L: ¿En tus días has dado órdenes a la mañana? \q ¿Has hecho saber a la aurora su lugar,
es.B: ¿Alguna vez en tu vida has dado órdenes a la mañana \q o le has mostrado a la aurora su lugar,
es.R: ¿Alguna vez en tu vida le has dicho a la mañana que empiece? \q ¿Le has mostrado a la aurora por dónde salir?

fr.L: De tes jours, as-tu donné un ordre au matin ? \q As-tu appris à l’aube [quelle est] sa place,
fr.B: As-tu jamais, de ta vie, donné des ordres au matin \q ou indiqué à l’aube sa place,
fr.R: As-tu une seule fois dans ta vie dit au matin de commencer ? \q As-tu montré à l’aube où elle doit paraître ?

sw.L: Je, katika siku zako uliipa asubuhi amri? \q Umeifanya alfajiri ijue mahali pake,
sw.B: Je, umewahi maishani mwako kuipa asubuhi amri \q au kuionyesha alfajiri mahali pake,
sw.R: Je, hata mara moja maishani mwako umewahi kuiambia asubuhi ianze? \q Umeionyesha alfajiri mahali pa kutokea?

vi.L: Từ những ngày của ngươi, ngươi đã ra lệnh cho buổi sáng chăng? \q Ngươi đã khiến rạng đông biết chỗ của nó,
vi.B: Đã bao giờ trong đời ngươi ra lệnh cho buổi sáng \q hay chỉ cho rạng đông chỗ của nó,
vi.R: Có lần nào trong đời ngươi bảo buổi sáng bắt đầu chưa? \q Ngươi có chỉ cho bình minh nơi phải ló dạng không?

ko.L: 너는 네가 사는 날 동안 아침에게 명령을 내린 적이 있느냐? \q 새벽이 제자리를 알게 해 주었느냐,
ko.B: 너는 평생에 한 번이라도 아침에게 명령을 내려 보았느냐? \q 새벽에게 그 자리를 정해 주었느냐,
ko.R: 너는 평생 한 번이라도 아침에게 시작하라고 말해 보았느냐? \q 새벽에게 어디서 밝아 올지 알려 주었느냐?

pt.L: Nos teus dias deste ordens à manhã? \q Fizeste a aurora conhecer o seu lugar,
pt.B: Alguma vez na vida deste ordens à manhã \q ou mostraste à aurora o seu lugar,
pt.R: Alguma vez na vida mandaste a manhã começar? \q Mostraste à aurora onde ela deve aparecer,

decisions.choice: from your days: ever in your life
decisions.reason: "From your days" means since your days began, at any time in your life (1 Samuel 25:28). The question is not only about creation but about every morning since.

decisions.choice: the dawn's place: where the light first appears on the horizon
decisions.reason: The point on the eastern horizon where dawn breaks moves through the year. God assigns it its place each day, as a commander assigns a post.

decisions.choice: made the dawn know (the reading tradition)
alternatives: made known the dawn (the written consonants)
decisions.reason: The consonants as written and the vowels of the reading tradition divide the words slightly differently. The reading tradition, followed here, gives "have you made the dawn know its place"; the meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into verses 13-15
decisions.reason: Verses 13-15 tell what the dawn does: it grasps the earth and shakes the wicked out. Literal and Balanced end this verse with a comma.

source.text: לֶ֭אֱחֹז בְּכַנְפ֣וֹת הָאָ֑רֶץ וְיִנָּעֲר֖וּ רְשָׁעִ֣יםמִמֶּֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: to take hold on [the] corners of the earth, and are shaken [the] wicked from it?

en.L: to take hold of the corners of the earth, \q and the wicked are shaken out of it?
en.B: so that it seizes the earth by its edges \q and shakes the wicked out of it?
en.R: Then it takes hold of the earth by its edges, like a blanket, \q and shakes the wicked out of it.

es.L: para que se aferre a los bordes de la tierra \q y los malvados sean sacudidos de ella?
es.B: para que tome la tierra por sus orillas \q y sacuda de ella a los malvados?
es.R: Entonces toma la tierra por sus bordes, como una manta, \q y sacude de ella a los malvados.

fr.L: pour qu’elle tienne les pans de la terre \q et que les méchants soient secoués hors d’elle ?
fr.B: afin qu’elle saisisse la terre par ses bords \q et en fasse tomber les méchants en la secouant ?
fr.R: Alors elle prend la terre par les bords, comme une couverture, \q et elle secoue les méchants pour les faire tomber.

sw.L: ili kuyashika malukio ya dunia, \q na waovu wapukutike kutoka humo?
sw.B: ili iishike dunia kwa ncha zake \q na kuwakung'uta waovu watoke ndani yake?
sw.R: Kisha inaishika dunia kwa ncha zake, kama blanketi, \q na kuwakung'uta waovu waanguke.

vi.L: để nắm lấy các góc của trái đất, \q và những kẻ ác bị giũ ra khỏi nó?
vi.B: để nó túm lấy trái đất ở các mép \q và giũ bọn gian ác ra khỏi đó?
vi.R: Rồi bình minh nắm lấy các mép trái đất như nắm tấm chăn \q và giũ bọn gian ác ra khỏi đó.

ko.L: 땅의 모서리들을 움켜쥐어 \q 악인들이 그 땅에서 털려 나가게 하려고?
ko.B: 땅을 그 끝자락으로 잡아 흔들어 \q 악인들을 털어 내게 하였느냐?
ko.R: 그러면 새벽은 담요를 잡듯 땅의 가장자리를 잡고 \q 악한 사람들을 털어 낸다.

pt.L: para agarrar as bordas da terra, \q e os perversos são sacudidos dela?
pt.B: para que ela pegue a terra pelas bordas \q e sacuda dela os perversos?
pt.R: Então ela pega a terra pelas bordas, como um cobertor, \q e sacode dela os perversos.

decisions.choice: the corners of the earth: the earth pictured as a cloth or garment
decisions.reason: The word (kanaf) means a wing and so the hem or corner of a garment (Ruth 3:9; 1 Samuel 15:27). The dawn takes the earth by its corners like a sheet and shakes it, and the wicked fall out like dust.

decisions.choice: the wicked are shaken out: daylight ends the work of those who act in darkness
decisions.reason: Robbers, murderers and adulterers work at night and hide from the light (24:13-17). When dawn comes their cover is gone.

decisions.choice: the raised letter in "wicked"
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew manuscripts the letter ayin of "wicked" here and in verse 15 is written raised above the line. The reason is not known; it does not change the word or the meaning.

decisions.choice: like a blanket (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable makes the picture of a cloth explicit (m1), since "the corners of the earth" alone may suggest only distance.

source.text: תִּ֭תְהַפֵּךְ כְּחֹ֣מֶר חוֹתָ֑ם וְ֝יִֽתְיַצְּב֗וּ כְּמ֣וֹ לְבֽוּשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: It is changed like clay of a seal, and they stand out like a garment.

en.L: It is changed like clay [under] a seal, \q and [its features] stand out like a garment.
en.B: The earth takes shape like clay under a seal; \q its features stand out like the folds of a garment.
en.R: In the light the earth changes, like clay pressed with a seal, \q and everything on it stands out like the colors of a garment.

es.L: Se transforma como arcilla [bajo] un sello, \q y [sus rasgos] se destacan como un vestido.
es.B: La tierra toma forma como arcilla bajo un sello; \q sus rasgos resaltan como los pliegues de un vestido.
es.R: Con la luz la tierra cambia, como arcilla marcada con un sello, \q y todo lo que hay en ella resalta como los colores de un vestido.

fr.L: Elle se transforme comme l’argile [sous] le sceau, \q et [ses traits] se dressent comme un vêtement.
fr.B: La terre prend forme comme l’argile sous un sceau ; \q ses reliefs ressortent comme les plis d’un vêtement.
fr.R: Dans la lumière, la terre change, comme l’argile marquée par un sceau, \q et tout ce qui s’y trouve ressort comme les couleurs d’un vêtement.

sw.L: Inabadilika kama udongo [chini ya] muhuri, \q na [sura zake] zinajitokeza kama vazi.
sw.B: Dunia inapata umbo kama udongo chini ya muhuri; \q sura zake zinajitokeza kama mikunjo ya vazi.
sw.R: Katika mwanga dunia inabadilika, kama udongo uliobonyezwa kwa muhuri, \q na kila kitu juu yake kinaonekana wazi kama rangi za vazi.

vi.L: Nó biến đổi như đất sét [dưới] con dấu, \q và [các nét của nó] nổi lên như một tấm áo.
vi.B: Trái đất thành hình như đất sét dưới con dấu; \q các đường nét nổi bật như nếp gấp của tấm áo.
vi.R: Trong ánh sáng, trái đất đổi khác, như đất sét được đóng dấu, \q và mọi vật trên đó hiện rõ như màu sắc của tấm áo.

ko.L: 그것은 인장 [아래의] 진흙처럼 변하고, \q [그 모습들이] 옷처럼 드러난다.
ko.B: 땅은 인장을 찍은 진흙처럼 모양을 갖추고 \q 그 생김새는 옷의 주름처럼 뚜렷해진다.
ko.R: 빛 속에서 땅은 도장을 찍은 진흙처럼 달라지고 \q 그 위의 모든 것이 옷의 색깔처럼 뚜렷이 드러난다.

pt.L: Ela se transforma como barro [sob] o selo, \q e [os seus contornos] se destacam como uma veste.
pt.B: A terra toma forma como o barro sob o selo; \q os seus contornos se destacam como as dobras de uma roupa.
pt.R: Com a luz a terra muda, como barro marcado por um selo, \q e tudo o que há nela se destaca como as cores de uma roupa.

decisions.choice: clay of a seal: clay that takes a clear image when a seal is pressed into it
decisions.reason: Documents and jars were closed with a lump of clay stamped with a seal (1 Kings 21:8). In the dark the earth has no shape; at dawn it takes clear form, as plain clay shows a design when the seal is pressed into it.

decisions.choice: they stand out: the earth's features
alternatives: it is dyed like a garment (a slightly different reading)
decisions.reason: The plural verb has no stated subject. Most likely it is the features of the earth, hills, trees and buildings, which stand out in the morning light like the pattern on a garment. Some take it of the wicked, who stand exposed; others read the verb with a small change as "it is dyed", the earth taking color like cloth.

decisions.choice: the earth ... its features (B); everything on it (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subjects the Hebrew leaves unstated (m2); Literal brackets them.

source.text: וְיִמָּנַ֣ע מֵרְשָׁעִ֣יםאוֹרָ֑ם וּזְר֥וֹעַ רָ֝מָ֗ה תִּשָּׁבֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And is withheld from [the] wicked their light, and [the] arm uplifted is broken.

en.L: And from the wicked their light is withheld, \q and the uplifted arm is broken.
en.B: The wicked are denied their light, \q and the arm they raise is broken.
en.R: The wicked lose the darkness that is their daylight, \q and the arm they raise to strike is broken.

es.L: Y se retiene de los malvados su luz, \q y el brazo alzado se quiebra.
es.B: A los malvados se les quita su luz, \q y el brazo que alzan se quiebra.
es.R: Los malvados pierden la oscuridad que es su luz del día, \q y el brazo que levantan para golpear queda roto.

fr.L: Et aux méchants leur lumière est retenue, \q et le bras levé se brise.
fr.B: Les méchants se voient retirer leur lumière, \q et le bras qu’ils lèvent se casse.
fr.R: Les méchants perdent l’obscurité qui leur sert de jour, \q et le bras qu’ils lèvent pour frapper est cassé.

sw.L: Na waovu wanazuiliwa nuru yao, \q na mkono ulionyanyuliwa unavunjwa.
sw.B: Waovu wananyimwa nuru yao, \q na mkono wanaouinua unavunjika.
sw.R: Waovu wanapoteza giza ambalo ndilo mchana wao, \q na mkono wanaouinua ili kupiga unavunjika.

vi.L: Và từ kẻ ác, ánh sáng của chúng bị giữ lại, \q và cánh tay vung cao bị gãy.
vi.B: Kẻ ác bị tước mất ánh sáng của chúng, \q và cánh tay chúng giơ lên bị bẻ gãy.
vi.R: Kẻ ác mất đi bóng tối vốn là ban ngày của chúng, \q và cánh tay chúng giơ lên để đánh người bị bẻ gãy.

ko.L: 악인들에게서는 그들의 빛이 막히고 \q 쳐든 팔은 부러진다.
ko.B: 악인들은 자기들의 빛을 빼앗기고 \q 그들이 휘두르는 팔은 부러진다.
ko.R: 악한 사람들은 낮과 같던 어둠을 잃고 \q 남을 치려고 쳐든 팔은 부러진다.

pt.L: E dos perversos é retida a sua luz, \q e o braço levantado é quebrado.
pt.B: Aos perversos é negada a sua luz, \q e o braço que eles levantam é quebrado.
pt.R: Os perversos perdem a escuridão que é a luz do dia deles, \q e o braço que levantam para ferir é quebrado.

decisions.choice: their light: the darkness that serves the wicked as light
decisions.reason: For the wicked, darkness is their morning (24:17): they do their work at night. When the dawn comes, that "light" of theirs is taken away. The words could also mean that the wicked, as punishment, are denied the light; the first reading fits verses 13-14 better.

decisions.choice: the uplifted arm: power raised to do violence
decisions.reason: The raised arm is strength used against others (compare Psalm 10:15, "break the arm of the wicked"; Job 22:9). Daylight stops it.

decisions.choice: the darkness that is their daylight; to strike (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains what "their light" is (m1) and what the raised arm is for (m2).

source.text: הֲ֭בָאתָ עַד־נִבְכֵי־יָ֑ם וּבְחֵ֥קֶר תְּ֝ה֗וֹם הִתְהַלָּֽכְתָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Have you gone to [the] springs of [the] sea, and in the searching of [the] deep have you walked about?

en.L: Have you gone to the springs of the sea, \q or walked about in the recesses of the deep?
en.B: Have you gone down to the sources of the sea \q or walked through the hidden depths of the ocean?
en.R: Have you been down to where the sea's water springs up? \q Have you walked along the bottom of the ocean?

es.L: ¿Has ido hasta los manantiales del mar, \q o te has paseado por los recovecos del abismo?
es.B: ¿Has bajado hasta las fuentes del mar \q o recorrido las profundidades ocultas del océano?
es.R: ¿Has bajado hasta donde brota el agua del mar? \q ¿Has caminado por el fondo del océano?

fr.L: Es-tu allé jusqu’aux sources de la mer, \q ou as-tu marché dans les recoins de l’abîme ?
fr.B: Es-tu descendu jusqu’aux sources de la mer \q ou as-tu parcouru les profondeurs cachées de l’océan ?
fr.R: Es-tu descendu là où jaillit l’eau de la mer ? \q As-tu marché au fond de l’océan ?

sw.L: Je, umeenda mpaka kwenye chemchemi za bahari, \q au kuzunguka katika pembe zilizofichika za kilindi?
sw.B: Je, umeshuka hadi kwenye vyanzo vya bahari \q au umepita katika vina vilivyofichika vya bahari kuu?
sw.R: Je, umewahi kushuka mahali maji ya bahari yanapobubujika? \q Umewahi kutembea chini kabisa ya bahari?

vi.L: Ngươi đã đến tận các mạch nguồn của biển, \q hay dạo bước trong những nơi sâu thẳm của vực sâu chưa?
vi.B: Ngươi đã xuống tận nguồn nước của biển \q hay đi qua những đáy sâu kín giấu của đại dương chưa?
vi.R: Ngươi đã từng xuống nơi nước biển phun lên chưa? \q Ngươi đã đi dọc đáy đại dương chưa?

ko.L: 네가 바다의 샘들에까지 가 보았느냐? \q 심연의 깊숙한 곳을 거닐어 보았느냐?
ko.B: 너는 바다의 근원까지 내려가 보았느냐? \q 바다 밑 숨은 깊음 속을 걸어 보았느냐?
ko.R: 바닷물이 솟아나는 곳에 내려가 보았느냐? \q 바다 맨 밑바닥을 걸어 본 적이 있느냐?

pt.L: Foste até as nascentes do mar, \q ou andaste nos recessos do abismo?
pt.B: Desceste até as fontes do mar \q ou andaste pelas profundezas escondidas do oceano?
pt.R: Já desceste até o lugar onde brota a água do mar? \q Já andaste pelo fundo do oceano?

decisions.choice: springs: the sources from which the sea's water comes
decisions.reason: This word occurs only here. Its sense is taken from related words for springs and from the line: the sea was thought to be fed by springs in the deep (Genesis 7:11; Proverbs 8:28).

decisions.choice: the recesses of the deep: the hidden depths, reached only by searching
decisions.reason: The word (cheqer) means a searching out, and so the farthest places that must be searched to be found (11:7). "The deep" (tehom) is the great mass of waters below (Genesis 1:2; 7:11).

decisions.choice: the ocean (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "The deep" can mean any depth in English; Balanced and Readable name the sea's depths plainly.

source.text: הֲנִגְל֣וּ לְ֭ךָ שַׁעֲרֵי־מָ֑וֶת וְשַׁעֲרֵ֖י צַלְמָ֣וֶת תִּרְאֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Have been revealed to you [the] gates of death, and the gates of deep darkness have you seen?

en.L: Have the gates of death been revealed to you, \q or have you seen the gates of deep darkness?
en.B: Have the gates of death been opened to you? \q Have you seen the gates of the deepest darkness?
en.R: Has anyone shown you the gates of the land of death? \q Have you seen the doors to the place of darkness?

es.L: ¿Te han sido reveladas las puertas de la muerte, \q o has visto las puertas de la oscuridad profunda?
es.B: ¿Se te han abierto las puertas de la muerte? \q ¿Has visto las puertas de la más honda oscuridad?
es.R: ¿Alguien te ha mostrado las puertas del país de la muerte? \q ¿Has visto las puertas del lugar de las tinieblas?

fr.L: Les portes de la mort t’ont-elles été révélées, \q ou as-tu vu les portes de l’obscurité profonde ?
fr.B: Les portes de la mort se sont-elles ouvertes devant toi ? \q As-tu vu les portes des plus épaisses ténèbres ?
fr.R: Quelqu’un t’a-t-il montré les portes du pays de la mort ? \q As-tu vu les portes du lieu des ténèbres ?

sw.L: Je, malango ya mauti yamefunuliwa kwako, \q au umeiona milango ya giza nene?
sw.B: Je, malango ya kifo yamefunguliwa kwako? \q Umeyaona malango ya giza lililo kuu kuliko yote?
sw.R: Je, kuna mtu aliyekuonyesha malango ya nchi ya wafu? \q Umeiona milango ya mahali pa giza?

vi.L: Các cổng của sự chết có được tỏ ra cho ngươi không, \q hay ngươi đã thấy các cổng của tối tăm mịt mù chưa?
vi.B: Các cổng sự chết đã mở ra trước mặt ngươi chưa? \q Ngươi đã thấy các cổng của bóng tối thăm thẳm chưa?
vi.R: Có ai chỉ cho ngươi các cổng của cõi chết chưa? \q Ngươi đã thấy các cửa dẫn vào nơi tối tăm chưa?

ko.L: 죽음의 문들이 너에게 열려 보인 적이 있느냐, \q 아니면 캄캄한 어둠의 문들을 보았느냐?
ko.B: 죽음의 문들이 너에게 열린 적이 있느냐? \q 가장 깊은 어둠의 문들을 본 적이 있느냐?
ko.R: 죽음의 나라로 들어가는 문을 누가 너에게 보여 주더냐? \q 어둠의 땅으로 가는 문을 본 적이 있느냐?

pt.L: Foram-te reveladas as portas da morte, \q ou viste as portas da escuridão profunda?
pt.B: As portas da morte te foram abertas? \q Viste as portas da escuridão mais profunda?
pt.R: Alguém te mostrou as portas da terra da morte? \q Viste as portas do lugar da escuridão?

decisions.choice: the gates of death: death pictured as a city or realm with gates
decisions.reason: The realm of the dead was pictured as a place below, with gates through which the dead go in (Psalm 9:14; Isaiah 38:10). It lies beneath the waters of verse 16 (26:5-6).

decisions.choice: deep darkness
decisions.reason: The word (tsalmavet) means the deepest darkness, the gloom of the grave (3:5; 10:21-22). Its spelling suggests "shadow of death", the older rendering; here, beside "death", both ideas are present.

decisions.choice: the land of death; the place of darkness (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says the gates lead to a place, so the picture is clear (m1).

source.text: הִ֭תְבֹּנַנְתָּ עַד־רַחֲבֵי־אָ֑רֶץ הַ֝גֵּ֗ד אִם־יָדַ֥עְתָּ כֻלָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Have you understood to [the] broad spaces of [the] earth? Tell, if you know all of it.

en.L: Have you understood the breadth of the earth? \q Tell, if you know all of it.
en.B: Have you grasped how wide the earth is? \q Tell {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, if you know all this.
en.R: Do you understand how huge the earth is? \q Tell {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, if you know it all.

es.L: ¿Has comprendido las anchuras de la tierra? \q Declara, si la conoces toda.
es.B: ¿Has captado cuán ancha es la tierra? \q Dímelo, si sabes todo esto.
es.R: ¿Entiendes lo enorme que es la tierra? \q Dímelo, si lo sabes todo.

fr.L: As-tu compris les étendues de la terre ? \q Raconte, si tu la connais tout entière.
fr.B: As-tu saisi l’étendue de la terre ? \q Dis-le-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, si tu sais tout cela.
fr.R: Comprends-tu combien la terre est immense ? \q Dis-le-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, si tu sais tout.

sw.L: Je, umeitafakari hadi mapana ya dunia? \q Sema, kama unaijua yote.
sw.B: Je, umeelewa jinsi dunia ilivyo pana? \q Niambie, kama unajua haya yote.
sw.R: Je, unaelewa jinsi dunia ilivyo kubwa mno? \q Niambie, kama unajua yote.

vi.L: Ngươi đã hiểu thấu các khoảng rộng của trái đất chưa? \q Hãy nói đi, nếu ngươi biết hết.
vi.B: Ngươi có nắm được trái đất rộng lớn đến đâu không? \q Hãy nói cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} biết, nếu ngươi biết hết những điều ấy.
vi.R: Ngươi có hiểu trái đất mênh mông thế nào không? \q Hãy nói cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nghe, nếu ngươi biết hết.

ko.L: 네가 땅의 넓은 곳들까지 깨달았느냐? \q 네가 그것을 다 안다면 말하여라.
ko.B: 땅이 얼마나 넓은지 헤아려 보았느냐? \q 이 모든 것을 안다면 나에게 말해 보아라.
ko.R: 땅이 얼마나 큰지 너는 아느냐? \q 다 안다면 나에게 말해 보아라.

pt.L: Compreendeste a largura da terra? \q Declara, se sabes tudo isso.
pt.B: Entendeste quão larga é a terra? \q Diz-{{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, se sabes tudo isso.
pt.R: Entendes como a terra é imensa? \q Diz-{{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, se sabes tudo.

decisions.choice: understood the broad spaces: grasped the full extent of the earth
decisions.reason: The verb means to give careful attention to and so to understand. "Up to the broad spaces of the earth" means its whole width, to its farthest ends.

decisions.choice: all of it: the whole earth
decisions.reason: The pronoun is feminine and most naturally refers to the earth. It may also sum up everything asked so far.

decisions.choice: Tell me (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 4, English needs an object for "tell".

source.text: אֵי־זֶ֣ה הַ֭דֶּרֶךְ יִשְׁכָּן־א֑וֹר וְ֝חֹ֗שֶׁךְ אֵי־זֶ֥ה מְקֹמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Where [is] this the way [where] dwells light, and darkness, where [is] this its place,

en.L: Where [is] the way [to where] light dwells? \q And darkness, where [is] its place,
en.B: Where is the road to the place where light lives? \q And darkness, where is its home,
en.R: Where is the road to the place where light lives? \q And where does darkness stay?

es.L: ¿Dónde [está] el camino [hacia donde] mora la luz? \q Y la oscuridad, ¿dónde [está] su lugar,
es.B: ¿Dónde está el camino al lugar donde vive la luz? \q Y la oscuridad, ¿dónde tiene su casa,
es.R: ¿Dónde está el camino al lugar donde vive la luz? \q ¿Y dónde se queda la oscuridad?

fr.L: Où [est] le chemin [vers le lieu où] habite la lumière ? \q Et les ténèbres, où [est] leur place,
fr.B: Où est la route qui mène là où vit la lumière ? \q Et l’obscurité, où est sa maison,
fr.R: Où est la route vers le lieu où vit la lumière ? \q Et où l’obscurité reste-t-elle ?

sw.L: Iko wapi njia [iendayo] mahali nuru ikaapo? \q Na giza, liko wapi eneo lake,
sw.B: Iko wapi barabara iendayo mahali nuru inapoishi? \q Na giza, nyumbani kwake ni wapi,
sw.R: Njia ya kwenda mahali nuru inapoishi iko wapi? \q Na giza hukaa wapi?

vi.L: Đâu [là] con đường [đến nơi] ánh sáng cư ngụ? \q Còn bóng tối, đâu [là] chỗ của nó,
vi.B: Đâu là con đường dẫn đến nơi ánh sáng ở? \q Còn bóng tối, nhà của nó ở đâu,
vi.R: Ánh sáng sống ở đâu, đường đến đó ở đâu? \q Còn bóng tối trú ngụ chỗ nào?

ko.L: 빛이 거하는 곳으로 [가는] 길이 어디냐? \q 어둠은, 그 자리가 어디냐,
ko.B: 빛이 사는 곳으로 가는 길이 어디냐? \q 어둠은, 그 집이 어디에 있느냐,
ko.R: 빛이 사는 곳으로 가는 길이 어디에 있느냐? \q 어둠은 어디에 머무르느냐?

pt.L: Onde [está] o caminho [para onde] habita a luz? \q E a escuridão, onde [está] o seu lugar,
pt.B: Onde está o caminho para o lugar onde mora a luz? \q E a escuridão, onde é a sua casa,
pt.R: Onde está o caminho para o lugar onde a luz mora? \q E onde a escuridão fica?

decisions.choice: light and darkness have dwellings
decisions.reason: Light and darkness are pictured as living beings who each have a home they come from and go back to, morning and evening (Genesis 1:3-5; Job 26:10). Only one who knows the way there could lead them home (verse 20).

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into verse 20
decisions.reason: Verse 20 completes the question: "... that you may take it to its territory?" Literal and Balanced end this verse with a comma.

source.text: כִּ֣י תִ֭קָּחֶנּוּ אֶל־גְּבוּל֑וֹ וְכִֽי־תָ֝בִ֗ין נְתִיב֥וֹת בֵּיתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: that you may take it to its territory, and that you may discern [the] paths of its house?

en.L: that you may take it to its territory \q and that you may discern the paths to its house?
en.B: so that you could lead it to its territory \q and know the paths to its home?
en.R: Can you lead them back to their own lands? \q Do you know the paths to their homes?

es.L: para que la lleves a su territorio \q y para que disciernas las sendas de su casa?
es.B: para que pudieras guiarla a su territorio \q y conocer los senderos hacia su hogar?
es.R: ¿Puedes llevarlas de vuelta a sus tierras? \q ¿Conoces los caminos hacia sus casas?

fr.L: pour que tu l’emmènes vers son territoire \q et que tu discernes les sentiers de sa maison ?
fr.B: pour que tu puisses la conduire jusqu’à son domaine \q et connaître les sentiers qui mènent chez elle ?
fr.R: Peux-tu les ramener chacune dans son pays ? \q Connais-tu les chemins de leurs maisons ?

sw.L: kwamba wewe uichukue hadi eneo lake \q na kwamba uzitambue njia za kuelekea nyumba yake?
sw.B: ili uweze kuiongoza hadi eneo lake \q na kuzijua njia za kwenda nyumbani kwake?
sw.R: Je, unaweza kuzirudisha kila moja katika nchi yake? \q Unazijua njia za kwenda kwenye makao yao?

vi.L: để ngươi đem nó về địa phận của nó \q và để ngươi nhận ra các lối đi đến nhà nó?
vi.B: để ngươi có thể dẫn nó về lãnh thổ của nó \q và biết các lối đi về nhà nó?
vi.R: Ngươi có thể dẫn chúng trở về xứ của chúng không? \q Ngươi có biết đường về nhà của chúng không?

ko.L: 그리하여 네가 그것을 그 경계로 데려가며 \q 그 집으로 가는 길들을 알아보겠느냐?
ko.B: 네가 그것을 제 땅으로 데려가고 \q 그 집으로 가는 길을 알겠느냐?
ko.R: 너는 빛과 어둠을 제 땅으로 데려다줄 수 있느냐? \q 그들의 집으로 가는 길을 아느냐?

pt.L: para que a leves ao seu território \q e para que discirnas as veredas da sua casa?
pt.B: para que pudesses levá-la ao seu território \q e conhecer os caminhos da sua casa?
pt.R: Podes levá-las de volta às suas terras? \q Conheces os caminhos para as suas casas?

decisions.choice: that you may take it: purpose, said with irony
decisions.reason: The small word can mean "that" or "for". Read as "that", it asks whether Job knows the way well enough to lead light and darkness home; read as "for", it is ironic praise, as in verse 21. The meaning is the same: Job cannot.

decisions.choice: it: each of light and darkness
decisions.reason: The singular "it" points to each in turn of the two named in verse 19.

decisions.choice: them ... their (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence and refers to light and darkness together (m2).

source.text: יָ֭דַעְתָּ כִּי־אָ֣ז תִּוָּלֵ֑ד וּמִסְפַּ֖ר יָמֶ֣יךָ רַבִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: You know, for then you were born, and [the] number of your days [is] many!

en.L: You know, for then you were born, \q and the number of your days [is] great!
en.B: Surely you know, since you were already born then, \q and you have lived so many days!
en.R: Of course you know! You were born back then, \q and you have lived for ages!

es.L: Lo sabes, pues entonces naciste, \q ¡y el número de tus días [es] grande!
es.B: Seguro que lo sabes, pues ya habías nacido entonces, \q ¡y has vivido tantísimos días!
es.R: ¡Claro que lo sabes! Ya habías nacido en aquel tiempo, \q ¡y has vivido muchísimos años!

fr.L: Tu sais, car c’est alors que tu es né, \q et nombreux [sont] tes jours !
fr.B: Tu le sais sûrement, puisque tu étais déjà né à cette époque, \q et tu as vécu tant de jours !
fr.R: Bien sûr que tu le sais ! Tu étais déjà né en ce temps-là, \q et tu vis depuis une éternité !

sw.L: Wewe unajua, kwa sababu ndipo ulipozaliwa, \q na idadi ya siku zako [ni] nyingi!
sw.B: Hakika unajua, maana ulikwisha kuzaliwa zamani hizo, \q na umeishi siku nyingi mno!
sw.R: Ni wazi unajua! Wewe ulikuwa umeshazaliwa wakati huo, \q na umeishi tangu zamani sana!

vi.L: Ngươi biết, vì khi ấy ngươi đã sinh ra, \q và số ngày của ngươi thật nhiều!
vi.B: Hẳn ngươi biết, vì lúc ấy ngươi đã ra đời rồi, \q và ngươi đã sống biết bao nhiêu ngày!
vi.R: Dĩ nhiên ngươi biết! Hồi đó ngươi đã sinh ra rồi, \q và ngươi đã sống lâu lắm rồi!

ko.L: 너는 알겠지, 그때 네가 태어났으니, \q 네 날의 수가 많지 않으냐!
ko.B: 너는 분명 알겠지. 그때 너는 이미 태어나 있었으니까. \q 네가 살아온 날이 그토록 많으니!
ko.R: 물론 너는 알겠지! 너는 그때 벌써 태어나 있었고 \q 아주 오랫동안 살아왔으니 말이다!

pt.L: Tu sabes, pois então nasceste, \q e o número dos teus dias [é] grande!
pt.B: Certamente sabes, pois já tinhas nascido então, \q e já viveste tantos dias!
pt.R: É claro que sabes! Tu nasceste naquele tempo \q e já viveste muitíssimo tempo!

decisions.choice: you know, for then you were born: irony
decisions.reason: God answers his own questions with mock agreement: of course Job knows, since he was there at the beginning. The point is the opposite. Eliphaz had used the same kind of irony against Job (15:7: "Were you the first human born?").

decisions.choice: then: at the time of creation
decisions.reason: "Then" points back to the founding of the world and the first ordering of light and darkness (verses 4-20).

decisions.choice: Surely (B), Of course (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add a word that makes the irony plain in English (m1); Literal keeps the bare statement.

decisions.choice: "알겠지" ... "많지 않으냐"
decisions.reason: The mock agreement (m1) is kept in plain modern endings; the archaic -리라 / -도다 are avoided.

source.text: הֲ֭בָאתָ אֶל־אֹצְר֣וֹת שָׁ֑לֶג וְאֹצְר֖וֹת בָּרָ֣ד תִּרְאֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Have you gone into [the] storehouses of snow, and [the] storehouses of hail have you seen,

en.L: Have you entered the storehouses of the snow, \q or seen the storehouses of the hail,
en.B: Have you gone into the storerooms of the snow \q or seen the storerooms of the hail,
en.R: Have you been inside the places where I store the snow? \q Have you seen where I keep the hail?

es.L: ¿Has entrado en los depósitos de la nieve, \q o has visto los depósitos del granizo,
es.B: ¿Has entrado en los almacenes de la nieve \q o has visto los almacenes del granizo,
es.R: ¿Has estado dentro de los lugares donde guardo la nieve? \q ¿Has visto dónde tengo el granizo?

fr.L: Es-tu entré dans les entrepôts de la neige, \q ou as-tu vu les entrepôts de la grêle,
fr.B: Es-tu entré dans les réserves de la neige \q ou as-tu vu les réserves de la grêle,
fr.R: Es-tu déjà entré là où je garde la neige ? \q As-tu vu où je conserve la grêle ?

sw.L: Je, umeingia ndani ya hazina za theluji, \q au umeona hazina za mvua ya mawe,
sw.B: Je, umeingia katika maghala ya theluji \q au kuyaona maghala ya mvua ya mawe,
sw.R: Je, umewahi kuingia mahali ninapohifadhi theluji? \q Umeona ninapoweka mvua ya mawe?

vi.L: Ngươi đã vào các vựa chứa tuyết, \q hay đã thấy các vựa chứa mưa đá,
vi.B: Ngươi đã vào những nơi trữ tuyết \q hay thấy những nơi trữ mưa đá,
vi.R: Ngươi đã bao giờ vào nơi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cất giữ tuyết chưa? \q Ngươi đã thấy chỗ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trữ mưa đá chưa?

ko.L: 네가 눈을 쌓아 둔 창고들에 들어가 보았느냐, \q 또 우박을 쌓아 둔 창고들을 보았느냐,
ko.B: 너는 눈을 간직해 둔 저장고에 들어가 보았느냐, \q 우박을 넣어 둔 저장고를 본 적이 있느냐,
ko.R: 내가 눈을 쌓아 두는 곳에 들어가 본 적이 있느냐? \q 내가 우박을 넣어 두는 곳을 본 적이 있느냐?

pt.L: Entraste nos depósitos da neve, \q ou viste os depósitos do granizo,
pt.B: Já entraste nos depósitos da neve \q ou viste onde se guarda o granizo,
pt.R: Já estiveste nos lugares onde guardo a neve? \q Já viste onde guardo o granizo?

decisions.choice: storehouses: weather kept in stores in the sky
decisions.reason: The sky is pictured as having storerooms from which God brings out wind, rain, snow and hail (Deuteronomy 28:12; Psalm 135:7; Jeremiah 10:13). Only God has access to them.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into verse 23
decisions.reason: Verse 23 tells what the stores are kept for. Literal and Balanced end this verse with a comma.

decisions.choice: where I store ... where I keep (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the stores are God's, as verse 23 ("which I have reserved") shows.

source.text: אֲשֶׁר־חָשַׂ֥כְתִּי לְעֶת־צָ֑ר לְי֥וֹם קְ֝רָ֗ב וּמִלְחָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: which I have reserved for [the] time of distress, for [the] day of battle and war?

en.L: which I have held back for a time of trouble, \q for a day of battle and war?
en.B: which I keep in reserve for times of trouble, \q for days of battle and war?
en.R: I keep them for times of trouble, \q for days of battle and war.

es.L: los cuales retuve para un tiempo de aprieto, \q para un día de combate y guerra?
es.B: que guardo en reserva para los tiempos de apuro, \q para los días de combate y de guerra?
es.R: Los guardo para los tiempos difíciles, \q para los días de lucha y de guerra.

fr.L: que j’ai retenus pour le temps de la détresse, \q pour le jour du combat et de la guerre ?
fr.B: que je garde de côté pour les temps de détresse, \q pour les jours de lutte et de guerre ?
fr.R: Je les garde pour les temps de malheur, \q pour les jours de bataille et de guerre.

sw.L: ambazo nimezihifadhi kwa ajili ya wakati wa dhiki, \q kwa siku ya mapambano na vita?
sw.B: ambazo ninazihifadhi kwa nyakati za shida, \q kwa siku za mapambano na vita?
sw.R: Ninaziweka kwa ajili ya nyakati za shida, \q kwa siku za mapambano na vita.

vi.L: mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã giữ lại cho thời khốn quẫn, \q cho ngày xung trận và chiến tranh?
vi.B: là những thứ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cất giữ cho những lúc hoạn nạn, \q cho những ngày giao tranh và chiến trận?
vi.R: Ta cất chúng cho những lúc khốn khó, \q cho những ngày đánh nhau và chiến tranh.

ko.L: 그것들은 내가 환난의 때를 위하여, \q 전투와 전쟁의 날을 위하여 아껴 둔 것이 아니냐?
ko.B: 그것은 내가 고난의 때를 대비하여, \q 싸움과 전쟁의 날을 위해 쌓아 둔 것이다.
ko.R: 나는 그것들을 어려운 때를 위해, \q 싸움과 전쟁의 날을 위해 두었다.

pt.L: que eu retive para o tempo da angústia, \q para o dia da batalha e da guerra?
pt.B: que eu reservo para os tempos de angústia, \q para os dias de batalha e de guerra?
pt.R: Eu os guardo para os tempos difíceis, \q para os dias de batalha e de guerra.

decisions.choice: hail kept for battle: God's weapons
decisions.reason: Hail is a weapon in God's hand: it struck Egypt (Exodus 9:23-26), killed the Amorites as they fled (Joshua 10:11), and comes with God's anger in Isaiah 30:30. The stores of the sky are an armory.

decisions.choice: a time of distress: a time of trouble or attack
decisions.reason: The word (tsar) means narrowness, so distress, and also an enemy. The time is when God acts against enemies.

source.text: אֵי־זֶ֣ה הַ֭דֶּרֶךְ יֵחָ֣לֶק א֑וֹר יָפֵ֖ץ קָדִ֣ים עֲלֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: Where [is] this the way [where] is divided light, [where] scatters [the] east wind over [the] earth?

en.L: Where [is] the way [where] the light is divided, \q [where] the east wind is scattered over the earth?
en.B: By what way is the light parceled out, \q or the east wind spread across the earth?
en.R: Which road does the light take when it spreads out? \q How does the east wind blow across the whole earth?

es.L: ¿Por dónde [es] el camino [donde] se reparte la luz, \q [donde] se esparce el viento del este sobre la tierra?
es.B: ¿Por qué camino se distribuye la luz, \q o se extiende el viento del este por la tierra?
es.R: ¿Qué camino toma la luz cuando se extiende? \q ¿Cómo sopla el viento del este por toda la tierra?

fr.L: Où [est] le chemin [par où] la lumière se répartit, \q [par où] le vent d’est se répand sur la terre ?
fr.B: Par quelle voie la lumière est-elle distribuée, \q ou le vent d’est dispersé à travers la terre ?
fr.R: Quelle route la lumière prend-elle pour se répandre ? \q Comment le vent d’est souffle-t-il sur toute la terre ?

sw.L: Iko wapi njia [ambapo] nuru hugawanywa, \q [ambapo] upepo wa mashariki hutawanyika juu ya dunia?
sw.B: Ni kwa njia gani nuru hugawanywa, \q au upepo wa mashariki huenezwa duniani kote?
sw.R: Nuru hufuata njia gani inaposambaa? \q Upepo wa mashariki huvumaje katika dunia nzima?

vi.L: Đâu [là] con đường [nơi] ánh sáng được phân tán, \q [nơi] gió đông bị thổi tung khắp mặt đất?
vi.B: Ánh sáng được phân phát theo ngả nào, \q hay gió đông được rải khắp đất ra sao?
vi.R: Ánh sáng đi đường nào khi tỏa rộng ra? \q Gió đông thổi khắp mặt đất bằng cách nào?

ko.L: 빛이 나뉘는 [그] 길, \q 동풍이 땅 위에 흩어지는 [그 길이] 어디냐?
ko.B: 빛이 갈라져 나가는 길은 어디며, \q 동풍이 온 땅으로 퍼지는 길은 어디냐?
ko.R: 빛은 어느 길로 퍼져 나가느냐? \q 동풍은 어떻게 온 땅에 부느냐?

pt.L: Onde [está] o caminho [onde] se reparte a luz, \q [onde] o vento leste se espalha sobre a terra?
pt.B: Por qual caminho a luz se distribui, \q ou o vento leste se espalha pela terra?
pt.R: Qual é o caminho que a luz faz quando se espalha? \q Como o vento leste sopra sobre toda a terra?

decisions.choice: light: probably daylight, possibly lightning
decisions.reason: The word ('or) normally means light, and verse 19 has already asked where light lives. But in the weather of this section it may mean lightning, as Elihu used it (36:30, 32; 37:11, 15). Some read a different word, heat or mist, to match the wind of the next line.

decisions.choice: the east wind: the hot, dry wind from the desert
decisions.reason: The east wind blows from the desert, scorching and strong (Genesis 41:6; Job 27:21; Hosea 13:15). It seems to come from nowhere and spread everywhere; God asks Job where its road is.

decisions.choice: is divided, scatters: spread out over the land
decisions.reason: Both verbs describe something spread out from one point over a wide area. The second is active in form ("scatters") but has no object; it is the wind spreading itself.

source.text: מִֽי־פִלַּ֣ג לַשֶּׁ֣טֶף תְּעָלָ֑ה וְ֝דֶ֗רֶךְ לַחֲזִ֥יז קֹלֽוֹת׃

fr.B: Qui creuse un canal pour les trombes de pluie \q et un chemin pour l’orage,
fr.R: Qui creuse dans le ciel un canal pour la pluie qui tombe à verse \q et ouvre un chemin à l’orage,

sw.L: Ni nani aliyechimba mfereji kwa ajili ya mvua kubwa \q na njia kwa ajili ya tufani ya ngurumo,

vi.R: Ai đã khoét trên trời một con kênh cho mưa trút xuống \q và vạch đường cho cơn giông,

ko.L: 누가 쏟아지는 비를 위해 도랑을 파 주고 \q 천둥 치는 폭풍을 위해 길을 놓아,
ko.B: 누가 거센 빗줄기를 위해 수로를 깎아 내고 \q 뇌우를 위해 길을 닦아 주어,
ko.R: 누가 하늘에 물길을 파서 장대비를 쏟아지게 하고 \q 뇌우에게 길을 내주어,

pt.L: Quem abriu um canal para o aguaceiro \q e um caminho para a tempestade de trovões,
pt.B: Quem abre um canal para as torrentes de chuva \q e um caminho para a trovoada,
pt.R: Quem abre no céu um canal para a chuva forte \q e faz um caminho para a trovoada,

decisions.choice: cut a channel for the flood: rain pictured as water led along a dug channel
decisions.reason: The word for channel (te'alah) is used of a water conduit or ditch (1 Kings 18:32; 2 Kings 18:17). The rain pours down along the path God has cut for it, as water runs along a ditch.

decisions.choice: storm of thunders: the thunderstorm, its lightning and thunder
decisions.reason: The phrase occurs also in 28:26. The first word means a storm cloud or the flash in it; with "thunders" it is the whole storm of lightning and thunder.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into verses 26-27
decisions.reason: Verses 26-27 give the purpose: to bring rain where no one lives. Literal, Balanced and Readable end this verse with a comma.

decisions.choice: in the sky (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says where the channel is, so the picture is not of a ditch on the ground (m1).

decisions.choice: "tufani ya ngurumo" (L), "tufani ya radi" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The storm of thunders is kept apart from "dhoruba", which stands for the windstorm God speaks from (38:1).

vi.B: để đem mưa đến miền đất không người cư ngụ, \q đến chốn hoang mạc vắng bóng con người,

pt.R: para que chova numa terra onde ninguém vive, \q num deserto onde não há gente,

decisions.choice: God sends rain where no human lives
decisions.reason: Rain falls on the empty desert, where no one will plant or harvest. God's care for creation reaches places that serve no human purpose; the world is not ordered around humans alone, a point the speech goes on to make with the wild animals (38:39-39:30).

decisions.choice: no one, no human: any person
decisions.reason: The two words ('ish and 'adam) here mean any human being at all, not men in particular.

pt.R: para dar à terra seca e vazia toda a água de que ela precisa \q e fazer crescer ali capim fresco?

decisions.choice: waste and desolation: utterly desolate ground
decisions.reason: The two nouns are formed from the same root, a sound-play like "ruin and ruination" (30:3; Zephaniah 1:15). Together they mean land that is completely barren.

decisions.choice: the going forth of grass: the place where grass sprouts, the new growth
decisions.reason: The first word means a going out or a source. With "grass" it is the springing up of new grass. Some read a similar word, "dry land", to match the first line; the sense is close.

decisions.choice: soak (B), give all the water it needs (R)
decisions.reason: To "satisfy" ground is to give it water until it has enough; Balanced and Readable say so plainly.

en.R: Does the rain have a father? \q Who is the parent of the dewdrops?

es.R: ¿Acaso la lluvia tiene padre? \q ¿Quién trajo al mundo las gotas de rocío?

fr.R: Est-ce que la pluie a un père ? \q Qui est le parent des gouttes de rosée ?

sw.R: Mvua ina baba yeyote? \q Matone ya umande yana mzazi gani?

vi.R: Mưa có cha không? \q Ai là cha mẹ của những hạt sương?

ko.L: 비에게 아버지가 있느냐, \q 아니면 누가 이슬방울들의 아비가 되었느냐?

decisions.choice: a father for the rain: who brings the rain into being
decisions.reason: Verses 28-29 ask about the origin of rain, dew, ice and frost in the language of birth: a father (verse 28) and a womb (verse 29). No human and no other power gives birth to them; the answer the questions expect is God alone (Jeremiah 14:22).

decisions.choice: drops: the drops of dew
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here. It is usually taken as "drops", from a root meaning to gather; some take it as the stores from which dew comes. The sense of the line is unchanged.

source.text: מִבֶּ֣טֶן מִ֭י יָצָ֣א הַקָּ֑רַח וּכְפֹ֥ר שָׁ֝מַיִם מִ֣י יְלָדֽוֹ׃

fr.R: De quel ventre vient la glace ? \q Qui donne naissance au givre qui tombe du ciel ?

sw.R: Ni mama gani aliyezaa barafu? \q Ni nani anayezaa jalidi inayoshuka kutoka angani?

vi.L: Từ lòng ai mà băng đá ra đời? \q Còn sương muối trên trời, ai đã sinh ra?
vi.B: Băng giá được sinh ra từ dạ của ai? \q Và ai đã sinh ra sương muối của bầu trời?
vi.R: Băng đá từ bụng ai mà ra? \q Ai sinh ra sương muối rơi xuống từ trời?

ko.L: 누구의 모태에서 얼음이 나오느냐? \q 그리고 하늘의 흰 서리, 그것을 누가 낳느냐?

pt.R: De que ventre vem o gelo? \q Quem dá à luz a geada que cai do céu?

decisions.choice: womb, give birth: the language of a mother
decisions.reason: After the father of verse 28 the picture turns to a mother. Both pictures say only that rain and ice have an origin outside the human world; God is their source (Psalm 147:16-17).

decisions.choice: the frost of the heavens: the hoarfrost
decisions.reason: The word (kefor) is the white frost that forms overnight (Exodus 16:14; Psalm 147:16). It seems to come from the sky.

decisions.choice: "jalidi" for the hoarfrost
decisions.reason: The white frost that forms overnight (m2); "jalidi" is the common word, "sakitu" is older and little known.

vi.B: Nước hóa cứng như đá, \q và mặt vực sâu đông kết lại.
vi.R: Nước trở nên cứng như đá, \q và mặt biển sâu đóng băng.

ko.L: 물들이 돌처럼 숨어 버리고 \q 깊음의 낯이 하나로 묶인다.
ko.B: 물은 돌처럼 단단해지고 \q 깊은 물의 표면은 단단히 엉겨 붙는다.
ko.R: 물이 돌처럼 딱딱해지고 \q 깊은 바다의 겉면이 꽁꽁 언다.

pt.L: As águas se escondem [e ficam] como pedra, \q e a face do abismo se prende.
pt.B: As águas endurecem como pedra, \q e a superfície do abismo congela.
pt.R: A água fica dura como pedra, \q e a superfície do mar profundo congela.

decisions.choice: hide themselves: become hidden under ice, hard as stone
decisions.reason: The verb means to hide. The water hides under its own ice and becomes like stone. Snow and ice were known in the hill country and the deserts around Israel (6:16; 37:10).

decisions.choice: is seized together: freezes
decisions.reason: The verb means to capture or seize; in this form it means to hold one another fast (41:9). The surface of the water is locked into one solid sheet.

decisions.choice: harden, freezes (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give what the two pictures describe, water turning to ice; Literal keeps the verbs.

decisions.choice: « Comme la pierre les eaux se dissimulent »
alternatives: « Les eaux se cachent [et deviennent] comme la pierre »
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew order, the comparison first, and needs no bracket.

source.text: הַֽ֭תְקַשֵּׁר מַעֲדַנּ֣וֹת כִּימָ֑ה אֽוֹ־מֹשְׁכ֖וֹת כְּסִ֣יל תְּפַתֵּֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: Can you bind [the] bonds of Kimah, or [the] cords of Kesil can you loosen?

en.L: Can you tie the bonds of the Pleiades, \q or loosen the cords of Orion?
en.B: Can you tie together the cluster of the Pleiades \q or untie the belt of Orion?
en.R: Can you tie the stars of the Pleiades together? \q Can you loosen the ropes that hold Orion?

es.L: ¿Anudarás las ataduras de las Pléyades, \q o aflojarás los cordeles de Orión?
es.B: ¿Puedes unir el racimo de las Pléyades \q o desatar el cinturón de Orión?
es.R: ¿Puedes atar juntas las estrellas de las Pléyades? \q ¿Puedes soltar las cuerdas que sujetan a Orión?

fr.L: Attacheras-tu les attaches des Pléiades, \q ou desserreras-tu les cordes d’Orion ?
fr.B: Peux-tu resserrer l’amas des Pléiades \q ou défaire la ceinture d’Orion ?
fr.R: Peux-tu attacher ensemble les étoiles des Pléiades ? \q Peux-tu desserrer les cordes qui tiennent Orion ?

sw.L: Je, utafunga mafungo ya Kilimia, \q au utazifungua kamba za Orioni?
sw.B: Je, waweza kulifunga pamoja kundi la Kilimia \q au kuufungua mkanda wa Orioni?
sw.R: Je, unaweza kuzifunga pamoja nyota za Kilimia? \q Unaweza kulegeza kamba zinazomshikilia Orioni?

vi.L: Ngươi có thể buộc các dây ràng của sao Rua, \q hay tháo các dây thừng của sao Thần Nông chăng?
vi.B: Ngươi có thể buộc chòm sao Rua lại với nhau \q hay cởi đai lưng của sao Thần Nông không?
vi.R: Ngươi có buộc được các ngôi sao Rua lại với nhau không? \q Ngươi có nới được những sợi dây giữ sao Thần Nông không?

ko.L: 네가 묘성의 매듭을 묶을 수 있느냐, \q 삼성의 밧줄을 풀 수 있느냐?
ko.B: 너는 묘성의 별무리를 한데 묶을 수 있느냐? \q 삼성의 허리띠를 끌러 낼 수 있느냐?
ko.R: 너는 묘성의 별들을 한데 묶을 수 있느냐? \q 삼성을 붙들어 맨 밧줄을 느슨하게 할 수 있느냐?

pt.L: Podes atar os laços das Plêiades, \q ou soltar as cordas do Órion?
pt.B: Podes amarrar o aglomerado das Plêiades \q ou desatar o cinturão do Órion?
pt.R: Podes amarrar umas às outras as estrelas das Plêiades? \q Podes soltar as cordas que prendem o Órion?

decisions.choice: Kimah and Kesil: probably the Pleiades and Orion
decisions.reason: The two names occur together also in 9:9 and Amos 5:8. Kimah is generally taken to be the Pleiades, a tight cluster of stars, and Kesil to be Orion; the word kesil also means "fool". The identifications come from early tradition and are likely, but not certain.

decisions.choice: bonds, cords: what holds the stars in their groups
decisions.reason: The first word may mean bonds, from a root meaning to tie, or ornaments, from a root meaning delight. With "tie" and "loosen" and the "cords" of the second line, bonds fits best. The stars are pictured as tied together; only God can tie or untie them.

decisions.choice: the cluster (B), the belt (B), the ropes (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced points to what the bonds seem to describe, the cluster of the Pleiades and the line of stars in Orion; Readable keeps the plain picture of tying.

decisions.choice: as Plêiades; o Órion
decisions.reason: The two names are given as in 9:9 ("o Órion e as Plêiades"), the identifications m1 gives, so the reader meets the same stars. The popular Brazilian names for parts of them ("Sete-Estrelo", "Três Marias" for Orion's belt) are not used, since they name only part of each group.

source.text: הֲתֹצִ֣יא מַזָּר֣וֹת בְּעִתּ֑וֹ וְ֝עַ֗יִשׁ עַל־בָּנֶ֥יהָ תַנְחֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Can you bring out Mazzaroth in its season, and [the] Ayish with its sons can you guide them?

en.L: Can you bring out Mazzaroth in its season, \q or guide the Bear with its sons?
en.B: Can you bring out the constellations at their proper times \q or guide the Bear with its cubs?
en.R: Can you bring out the groups of stars each at the right time of year? \q Can you lead the Great Bear and the stars that follow it?

es.L: ¿Puedes sacar a Mazarot a su tiempo, \q o guiar a la Osa con sus hijos?
es.B: ¿Puedes hacer salir las constelaciones a su debido tiempo \q o guiar a la Osa con sus crías?
es.R: ¿Puedes hacer salir cada grupo de estrellas en su época del año? \q ¿Puedes guiar a la Osa Mayor y a las estrellas que la siguen?

fr.L: Peux-tu faire sortir Mazzaroth en sa saison, \q ou conduire l’Ourse avec ses fils ?
fr.B: Peux-tu faire paraître les constellations au moment voulu \q ou guider l’Ourse avec ses oursons ?
fr.R: Peux-tu faire apparaître chaque groupe d’étoiles à la bonne saison ? \q Peux-tu conduire la Grande Ourse et les étoiles qui la suivent ?

sw.L: Je, waweza kumtoa Mazarothi kwa wakati wake, \q au kumwelekeza Dubu na wana wake?
sw.B: Je, waweza kuyatokeza makundi ya nyota kwa nyakati zake \q au kumwongoza Dubu pamoja na vitoto vyake?
sw.R: Je, unaweza kutokeza kila kundi la nyota kwa majira yake ya mwaka? \q Unaweza kumwongoza Dubu Mkubwa na nyota zinazomfuata?

vi.L: Ngươi có thể dẫn Ma-xa-rốt ra theo mùa của nó, \q hay dẫn đường sao Bắc Đẩu cùng các con nó không?
vi.B: Ngươi có thể khiến các chòm sao mọc lên đúng thời \q hay dẫn dắt sao Bắc Đẩu cùng đàn con nó không?
vi.R: Ngươi có làm cho mỗi chòm sao xuất hiện đúng mùa trong năm không? \q Ngươi có dẫn được chòm Bắc Đẩu cùng những vì sao đi kèm không?

ko.L: 네가 마사롯을 제철에 내보낼 수 있느냐, \q 북두성을 그 아들들과 함께 인도할 수 있느냐?
ko.B: 너는 별자리들을 정한 때에 떠오르게 할 수 있느냐? \q 북두성을 그 새끼들과 함께 이끌 수 있느냐?
ko.R: 너는 별자리들이 저마다 알맞은 철에 나타나게 할 수 있느냐? \q 북두칠성과 그 뒤를 따르는 별들을 이끌 수 있느냐?

pt.L: Podes fazer sair Mazarote no seu tempo, \q ou guiar a Ursa com os seus filhos?
pt.B: Podes fazer surgir as constelações no tempo certo \q ou guiar a Ursa com os seus filhotes?
pt.R: Podes fazer aparecer cada grupo de estrelas na época certa do ano? \q Podes conduzir a Ursa Maior e as estrelas que a seguem?

decisions.choice: Mazzaroth: a star group not now known; perhaps the constellations or the signs of the zodiac
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here. It may be the same as a word in 2 Kings 23:5 for the constellations or the signs of the zodiac; others take it as one particular star group. What it names is not known. Literal keeps the name.

decisions.choice: Ayish with its sons: probably the Great Bear with the stars around it
decisions.reason: Ayish (compare 'Ash in 9:9) is identified in early tradition with the Great Bear, whose "sons" would be its smaller stars; others have suggested the star Aldebaran with the Hyades. The identification is uncertain.

decisions.choice: in its season: at its appointed time of year
decisions.reason: Constellations rise and set at fixed times of the year; God brings each out when its time comes (compare verse 33).

decisions.choice: Mazzaroth (L), the constellations (B), the groups of stars (R); the Bear (L, B), the Great Bear (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the unknown name Mazzaroth; Balanced and Readable give the likeliest general sense (m1). All levels name the Bear as the likeliest identification (m2).

decisions.choice: «Mazarot» at Literal
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the unknown name, transcribed (m1); Balanced and Readable give the general sense.

decisions.choice: « Mazzaroth » at Literal
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the unknown name (m1); Balanced and Readable give the general sense.

decisions.choice: "Mazarothi" at Literal
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the unknown name, transcribed (m1); Balanced and Readable give the general sense.

decisions.choice: "Ma-xa-rốt" at Literal
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the unknown name, transcribed (m1); Balanced and Readable give the general sense.

decisions.choice: "마사롯" at Literal; "북두칠성" at Readable
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the unknown name, transcribed (m1). Readable names the Great Bear by its everyday name 북두칠성; Literal and Balanced keep 북두성 as in 9:9.

decisions.choice: Mazarote (L), as constelações (B), cada grupo de estrelas (R); a Ursa (L, B), a Ursa Maior (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the unknown name in a Portuguese spelling, "Mazarote" (m1), as the English Literal keeps "Mazzaroth". "A Ursa" is the name used in 9:9 for the related star name; Readable says "a Ursa Maior", as the English Readable says "the Great Bear" here, the identification m2 calls probable.

source.text: הֲ֭יָדַעְתָּ חֻקּ֣וֹת שָׁמָ֑יִם אִם־תָּשִׂ֖ים מִשְׁטָר֣וֹ בָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: Do you know [the] statutes of [the] heavens? Or can you set its rule on the earth?

en.L: Do you know the statutes of the heavens? \q Or can you set its rule on the earth?
en.B: Do you know the laws that govern the heavens? \q Can you establish their rule over the earth?
en.R: Do you know the laws that control the sky? \q Can you make them rule over the earth?

es.L: ¿Conoces los estatutos de los cielos? \q ¿O puedes establecer su dominio sobre la tierra?
es.B: ¿Conoces las leyes que rigen los cielos? \q ¿Puedes establecer su dominio sobre la tierra?
es.R: ¿Conoces las leyes que gobiernan el cielo? \q ¿Puedes hacer que gobiernen la tierra?

fr.L: Connais-tu les statuts des cieux ? \q Ou peux-tu établir leur pouvoir sur la terre ?
fr.B: Connais-tu les lois qui règlent les cieux ? \q Peux-tu leur donner autorité sur la terre ?
fr.R: Connais-tu les lois qui commandent le ciel ? \q Peux-tu les faire régner sur la terre ?

sw.L: Je, unayajua maagizo ya mbingu? \q Au unaweza kuuweka utawala wake juu ya nchi?
sw.B: Je, unajua sheria zinazotawala mbingu? \q Je, unaweza kuuweka utawala wake juu ya dunia?
sw.R: Je, unazijua sheria zinazoongoza anga? \q Unaweza kuzifanya zitawale dunia?

vi.L: Ngươi có biết các định luật của trời không? \q Hay ngươi đặt được sự thống trị của nó trên đất?
vi.B: Ngươi có biết các luật điều khiển bầu trời không? \q Ngươi có thể thiết lập quyền cai trị của chúng trên đất không?
vi.R: Ngươi có biết những luật lệ chi phối bầu trời không? \q Ngươi có thể khiến chúng cai quản mặt đất không?

ko.L: 네가 하늘의 법칙들을 아느냐? \q 네가 그 다스림을 땅에 세울 수 있느냐?
ko.B: 너는 하늘을 다스리는 법칙들을 아느냐? \q 그 법칙들이 땅을 다스리게 할 수 있느냐?
ko.R: 너는 하늘을 움직이는 법칙을 아느냐? \q 그것들이 땅을 다스리게 할 수 있느냐?

pt.L: Conheces os estatutos dos céus? \q Ou podes estabelecer o seu domínio sobre a terra?
pt.B: Conheces as leis que governam os céus? \q Podes estabelecer o domínio deles sobre a terra?
pt.R: Conheces as leis que controlam o céu? \q Podes fazer que elas governem a terra?

decisions.choice: the statutes of the heavens: the fixed order of the sky
decisions.reason: The word (chuqqot) means fixed decrees. The sun, moon and stars keep their courses by God's decrees (Jeremiah 31:35-36; 33:25).

decisions.choice: its rule: the heavens' influence over the earth
decisions.reason: This word occurs only here; it is related to the word for an officer or overseer. The order of the sky governs the seasons and times on earth (Genesis 1:14-18). God asks whether Job can set that order in place.

decisions.choice: their rule (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "its" refers to the heavens; Balanced and Readable say "their", following the English plural.

source.text: הֲתָרִ֣ים לָעָ֣ב קוֹלֶ֑ךָ וְֽשִׁפְעַת־מַ֥יִם תְּכַסֶּֽךָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Can you lift up to the cloud your voice, and an abundance of water cover you?

en.L: Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, \q so that a flood of waters covers you?
en.B: Can you shout an order to the clouds \q and have a flood of water cover you?
en.R: Can you call out to the clouds \q and make them pour down rain on you?

es.L: ¿Levantarás hacia la nube tu voz, \q y una crecida de aguas te cubrirá?
es.B: ¿Puedes dar órdenes a gritos a las nubes \q y hacer que una inundación de agua te cubra?
es.R: ¿Puedes llamar a las nubes \q y hacer que te caiga encima un aguacero?

fr.L: Peux-tu lever ta voix vers la nuée, \q et qu’un déluge d’eaux te recouvre ?
fr.B: Peux-tu crier un ordre aux nuages \q et faire qu’un déluge d’eau te recouvre ?
fr.R: Peux-tu appeler les nuages \q et les faire pleuvoir sur toi ?

sw.L: Je, utapaza sauti yako kwa wingu, \q na maji mengi yakufunike?
sw.B: Je, unaweza kuyapigia mawingu kelele ya amri \q na mafuriko ya maji yakakufunika?
sw.R: Je, unaweza kuyaita mawingu \q na kuyafanya yakumwagie mvua?

vi.L: Ngươi có thể lên giọng gọi mây, \q để nước dồi dào bao phủ ngươi không?
vi.B: Ngươi có thể hô truyền lệnh cho mây \q để nước lũ tràn phủ trên ngươi không?
vi.R: Ngươi có gọi được mây \q và khiến chúng đổ mưa trên ngươi không?

ko.L: 네가 구름에게 소리를 질러 \q 많은 물이 너를 덮게 할 수 있느냐?
ko.B: 너는 구름에게 큰 소리로 명령하여 \q 물이 홍수처럼 너를 뒤덮게 할 수 있느냐?
ko.R: 너는 구름을 불러 \q 너에게 비를 퍼붓게 할 수 있느냐?

pt.L: Podes levantar a tua voz até as nuvens, \q para que uma inundação de águas te cubra?
pt.B: Podes dar uma ordem em voz alta às nuvens \q e fazer que uma enxurrada de águas te cubra?
pt.R: Podes chamar as nuvens \q e fazer que elas derramem chuva sobre ti?

decisions.choice: and an abundance covers you: the result of the command
decisions.reason: The second line tells what would follow if the clouds obeyed: a downpour. Can Job command rain, as God does?

decisions.choice: an abundance of water covers you: the phrase of 22:11
decisions.reason: Eliphaz used the same words of the flood that would overwhelm Job as punishment (22:11). Here the flood is rain that only God can call down.

decisions.choice: shout an order (B), call out (R)
decisions.reason: To "lift up the voice" means to call aloud; here it is a command to the clouds.

decisions.choice: uma inundação de águas te cubra (L); uma enxurrada de águas te cubra (B)
decisions.reason: The words are those of Eliphaz's threat in 22:11 (m2), so Literal and Balanced use the Portuguese of that verse at the same level ("uma inundação de águas cobre você", "uma enxurrada de águas"), and the reader hears God turn the picture around.

source.text: הַֽתְשַׁלַּ֣ח בְּרָקִ֣ים וְיֵלֵ֑כוּ וְיֹאמְר֖וּ לְךָ֣ הִנֵּֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Can you send out lightnings, and they will go and say to you, Here we [are]?

en.L: Can you send out lightning bolts so that they go \q and say to you, 'Here we [are]'?
en.B: Can you send the lightning bolts on their way, \q and will they say to you, 'Here we are'?
en.R: Can you send out the lightning? \q Does it come to you and say, 'We are ready'?

es.L: ¿Puedes enviar relámpagos para que vayan \q y te digan: “Aquí [estamos]”?
es.B: ¿Puedes enviar los rayos en su camino, \q y te dirán: “Aquí estamos”?
es.R: ¿Puedes mandar los relámpagos? \q ¿Vienen a ti y te dicen: “Estamos listos”?

fr.L: Envoies-tu les éclairs pour qu’ils partent \q et te disent : “Nous voici” ?
fr.B: Peux-tu lancer les éclairs sur leur route, \q et te diront-ils : “Nous voici” ?
fr.R: Peux-tu envoyer les éclairs ? \q Viennent-ils te dire : “Nous sommes prêts” ?

sw.L: Je, utatuma miale ya radi nayo ikaenda, \q ikakwambia, 'Sisi hapa'?
sw.B: Je, unaweza kuituma miale ya radi iende zake, \q nayo ikwambie, 'Tuko hapa'?
sw.R: Je, unaweza kutuma radi? \q Inakujia na kukwambia, 'Tuko tayari'?

vi.L: Ngươi có sai được các tia chớp để chúng lên đường \q và nói với ngươi: 'Có chúng tôi đây' không?
vi.B: Ngươi có thể sai các lằn chớp đi làm việc, \q và chúng sẽ thưa với ngươi: 'Chúng tôi đến rồi' chăng?
vi.R: Ngươi có sai được chớp không? \q Chớp có đến bảo ngươi: 'Chúng tôi sẵn sàng' không?

ko.L: 번개들을 네가 내보내면 그것들이 떠나가서 \q '저희가 여기 있습니다' 하고 너에게 아뢰겠느냐?
ko.B: 너는 번개를 내보내 제 길을 가게 할 수 있느냐? \q 번개가 너에게 '여기 대령했습니다' 하고 말하겠느냐?
ko.R: 너는 번개를 보낼 수 있느냐? \q 번개가 너에게 와서 '준비되었습니다' 하고 말하느냐?

pt.L: Podes enviar relâmpagos, para que vão \q e te digam: 'Eis-nos [aqui]'?
pt.B: Podes mandar os relâmpagos seguirem o seu caminho, \q e eles te dirão: 'Aqui estamos'?
pt.R: Podes enviar os relâmpagos? \q Eles vêm a ti e dizem: 'Estamos prontos'?

decisions.choice: here we are: the answer of a servant ready to obey
decisions.reason: "Here I am" is the reply of one who stands ready for orders (Genesis 22:1; 1 Samuel 3:4; Isaiah 6:8). The lightning bolts are pictured as servants who report for duty to the one who sent them.

decisions.choice: they go and say: lightning as messengers
decisions.reason: The lightning goes out on its errand and reports back. God sends it where he wills (37:3, 11-12).

decisions.choice: We are ready (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the servant's reply (m1).

source.text: מִי־שָׁ֭ת בַּטֻּח֣וֹת חָכְמָ֑ה א֤וֹ מִֽי־נָתַ֖ן לַשֶּׂ֣כְוִי בִינָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Who has put in the inward parts wisdom, or who has given to the mind understanding?

en.L: Who has put wisdom in the inward parts, \q or who has given understanding to the mind?
en.B: Who has put wisdom in the inner self \q or given understanding to the mind?
en.R: Who gives wisdom to the heart? \q Who gives understanding to the mind?

es.L: ¿Quién puso sabiduría en las entrañas, \q o quién dio a la mente inteligencia?
es.B: ¿Quién ha puesto sabiduría en lo íntimo del ser \q o ha dado entendimiento a la mente?
es.R: ¿Quién da sabiduría al corazón? \q ¿Quién da entendimiento a la mente?

fr.B: Qui a mis la sagesse au fond de l’être \q ou donné à la pensée l’intelligence ?

decisions.choice: the inward parts: the hidden inner self
decisions.reason: This rare word appears elsewhere only in Psalm 51:8, "truth in the inward parts". Here, among questions about the sky, some take it as a bird, the ibis, believed in Egypt to know when the Nile would rise, or as a feature of the clouds. The inner self fits Psalm 51:8 and the word "wisdom".

decisions.choice: the mind
decisions.reason: This word occurs only here. Later Hebrew used it for the rooster, which announces the dawn, and the Jewish morning blessing gives thanks to God "who gave the rooster understanding". If the first line speaks of a bird, this one may too; if of the inner self, this word is the mind.

decisions.choice: the heart (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable uses the common English word for the inner self.

decisions.choice: the jars of heaven: the clouds as water jars
decisions.reason: The word (nevel) means a large jar or a skin for wine or water (1 Samuel 1:24; 10:3). The rain clouds are pictured as jars that God tips over to pour out rain.

decisions.choice: count by wisdom: know and order the clouds
decisions.reason: To number something is to know it fully and have it in hand (Psalm 147:4, of the stars). Wisdom (verse 36) is needed to manage the clouds.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into verse 38
decisions.reason: Verse 38 says when the jars are tipped. Literal ends this verse with a comma; Balanced and Readable run on without a stop.

decisions.choice: water jars (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the jars hold (m1).

decisions.choice: a cast mass: like metal poured into a mold
decisions.reason: The word is from the verb "pour, cast" and is used of cast metal (1 Kings 7:37; Job 37:18). The dust lies hard and solid like a casting.

decisions.choice: when: in drought, before the rain
alternatives: after the rain, when wet dust turns to mud
decisions.reason: The verse most likely describes the dry ground baked hard, the moment when God tips the jars of the sky (verse 37). It could also describe the dust turned to mud and caked together after the rain has fallen.

decisions.choice: the speech turns to the animals

decisions.choice: lion, young lions: a lion or lioness, and lions old enough to hunt
decisions.reason: The first word (lavi') may be a lion or a lioness (Genesis 49:9); the second (kefirim) is young lions in their full strength, able to hunt (4:10-11).

decisions.choice: appetite: hunger
decisions.reason: The word means life, and here, as in 33:20, the desire for food.

decisions.choice: the lioness (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Among lions the female does most of the hunting for the young; Balanced takes the word in that sense. Literal keeps "lion".

decisions.choice: the young ravens cry to God
decisions.reason: God feeds even the raven, an unclean bird (Leviticus 11:15), when its young cry. Psalm 147:9 says the same, and Jesus points to the ravens fed by God (Luke 12:24).

decisions.choice: its prey: food got by hunting
decisions.reason: The word (tsayid) means game or prey. The raven eats what it finds or scavenges.

decisions.choice: wander about: stagger, flutter helplessly
decisions.reason: The verb means to wander or stagger. The young birds, weak with hunger, flutter about the nest.
